nodes.label: Multi-Game Digimon Vault and Transfer Plan
Binding Product Contract (2026-10-17)
nodes.rationale: Supersedes earlier mode, archive-first presentation and base-only DIM wording; PKVault/PKForge are interaction references for a universal Digimon home spanning games and V-Pets, not limits on the destination set.

nodes.label: Zero-Progress A/B/C/A Round-Trip Invariant
nodes.rationale: For Game A -> Storage -> Game B -> Storage -> Game C -> Storage -> Game A with no progress made, the individual must be returnable to Game A with the same native stats it had when it left; lossy intermediate projections must not fabricate gains, compound rounding loss or destroy the original baseline.

nodes.label: Universal Progress Translation and Balanced Origin Influence
VB-first / Dot-first Artwork Priority
nodes.rationale: Gameplay mode and source/artwork participation gates were removed because the only remaining replacement choice is cosmetic: changing the preference cannot clear the active partner, pause activities, alter stats or invalidate play, and a missing sprite cannot block a supported native transfer.

nodes.label: Farm Records Inspection-Only Scope
nodes.rationale: Farm Digimon do not need to be transferable and resolving farm identity/occupancy is not a dependency for party/bank transfer, so farm references are optional research rather than required acceptance gates.

nodes.label: Save-Reading Standard
nodes.rationale: Any structurally recognizable save must be readable regardless of game point, file name or folder, because users rely on arbitrary emulator and PC save layouts; write safety stays independent of read tolerance and each new reader must demonstrate the standard before shipping.

nodes.label: Writer Ladder (rung-1 NOOP_REWRITE)
nodes.rationale: Writers advance one rung at a time, starting from an identical rewrite and no-op insert/remove, because saves could be corrupted and capability flags must stay declared false until the game itself accepts each rung.

nodes.label: Standing evidence rule
nodes.rationale: A JVM, compile or loopback result is never accepted as evidence of game, device, writer or platform behavior; phase acceptance must use the strongest available evidence class and label it explicitly.
